prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, close-up beauty portrait. ONE woman, facing the camera straight on in a perfectly frontal portrait, her head level, both ears clearly visible on either side of her face, framed tightly from the very top of her head down to the line of her shoulders, the frame cutting off just below them, so the weights fully hang in view. Her face is large and sharp. Early 50s.

Subject: A real photograph of a striking adult Japanese woman — Japanese poised refined beauty light-neutral complexion with a soft peach-beige undertone, early 50s, long straight silver hair with a side part, very dewy glass skin with a strong highlight on the cheekbones, nose bridge and forehead, a rosy blush, glossy coral lips, odd-eyed with two clearly different lenses: her left eye has a bright turquoise coloured contact lens with round natural pupils, fully opaque and solidly saturated across the whole iris with no natural brown showing through, the colour bright and unmistakable, with a darker limbal ring, and her right eye has a deep cobalt-blue coloured contact lens with a vertical slit cat-eye pupil, fully opaque and solidly saturated across the whole iris with no natural brown showing through, the colour bright and unmistakable, with a darker limbal ring, sitting naturally on the irises and clear of the eyelids, the two eye colours both bright and clearly different from each other, eyes opened extremely wide with the whites showing all around the irises, a fixed unblinking stare, brows raised, a wide stretched grin showing teeth, a manic, unhinged expression — a photograph of a real Japanese woman's face, not an illustration, not a render. She has no eyebrows at all: her brow bones are completely smooth, bare, clean skin with no hair, no drawing and no ornament, like the face of the Mona Lisa, so the whole attention rests on her eyes. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living skin with visible pores and faint peach-fuzz hairs, slightly asymmetrical with a few small natural beauty marks and freckles, never airbrushed and never smooth like plastic, real wet catchlights in the eyes, individual hair strands catching the light. Her face has been surgically sculpted far beyond her natural look, and these changes override her natural features: her eyes are the star of her face (the shape, size and lenses described here override the eyes of her makeup, while the colours of her eyeshadow and liner follow her makeup): extremely heavy-lidded, almost closed, smouldering eyes with a very deep-set heavy upper lid covering about half of the iris, dramatic dark smoky brown-black eyeshadow blended up to the brow bone, extremely thick long curled lashes resting on the lid and a long sharp winged liner, in rich dark-brown contact lenses with a little warm hazel glow, both eyes the same, with a round natural pupil and bright catchlights; her nose: a high, straight, refined, surgically sculpted nose: a tall, slim, straight bridge, a narrow, pointed, projecting tip and clearly narrow nostril wings with slim, neat nostrils; her jawline and chin: a heart-shaped face: a wide forehead and high, full cheekbones narrowing in a smooth curve into a delicate, pointed, softly rounded chin like the tip of a heart. Every feature is exaggerated but beautiful, balanced and refined, in harmony with the rest of her face, never distorted, never grotesque.

Piercings: A face fully covered with real piercings, about eleven in total (not counting the hanging weights), spread over every area so that no area is empty: a single large septum ring of different sizes and shapes through the thin soft wall between the nostrils, in a short stack that ends above the upper lip; one small ring wrapping snugly around each nostril wing; one small hoop or stud along the edge of the upper lip; one small hoop or stud across the lower lip's edge; one small ring or stud on the chin; on each ear, three separate large healed openings in the earlobe, one below another with a clear gap of bare skin between each, each opening holding its own very thick, heavy black cast-iron ring as thick as a finger, a plain solid ring with no open tunnel, and above them sit zero thick classic round O-rings and studs along the helix rim above the lobe; one small stud across the lower half of the forehead just above the brows in even rows, leaving the upper forehead free; one small stud along each cheekbone, well clear of the eyes. Fine chains link the pieces: from the upper ear hoop on each side a delicate chain swags across the cheek to the ring around the nostril wing on the same side, passing well below the eye and clear of the lips, and one more fine chain hangs in a soft curve under the jaw from one ear to the other; the chains are thin enough that every piece and her whole face stay clearly visible. The left and right sides are balanced. The pieces are spread over the whole face in clear rows so every one reads individually, with bare skin between them; the eyes and eyelids stay clear. Stickers: five tiny glow-in-the-dark heart and star stickers are scattered flat on the skin of the lower cheeks and the jawline below the cheekbone studs, clear of the piercings, the eyes and the lips. All the ear weights hang from the bottoms of these three iron rings, and they are not counted in the piercing total: on each ear there are exactly nine separate massive weights, each of a different shape and a different metal, all of them rough, hammered, matte and unpolished, each hanging on its own thick heavy chain of the same metal as the weight: on the left ear oxidized dark copper a miniature anvil on a shortest chain, dull blue-grey lead a hammer head on a shortest chain, tarnished dark silver a square-sided cowbell on a short chain, dark patinated bronze a bell-shaped weight like a small temple bell with a flared rim on a medium chain, dull pewter-grey tin a round bell on a medium chain, rough-cast matte yellow gold a cube-shaped block on a long chain, dull dark brass a ship's anchor on a longer chain, blackened cast iron a chunky hexagonal nut-shaped weight with a round hole through the centre on a longer chain, dark patinated bronze a pyramid-shaped lump on a longest chain; on the right ear rough-cast matte yellow gold a pyramid-shaped lump on a shortest chain, tarnished dark silver a bell-shaped weight like a small temple bell with a flared rim on a shortest chain, oxidized dark copper a chunky hexagonal nut-shaped weight with a round hole through the centre on a short chain, dark patinated bronze a round bell on a medium chain, dull pewter-grey tin a cube-shaped block on a medium chain, dull dark brass a hammer head on a long chain, blackened cast iron a square-sided cowbell on a longer chain, dull blue-grey lead a miniature anvil on a longer chain, rough-cast matte yellow gold a barrel-shaped weight on a longest chain. On each ear the three iron rings share the weights between them in uneven numbers, each ring carrying its own column of weights, hanging side by side on chains of different lengths and staggered at different heights so every weight is fully visible and none hides another. Every single weight is a massive, dense, solid lump of metal at least as big as her whole fist and clearly larger than her earlobe, rough and matte and unpolished with no shine and no delicate or thin parts; its size does NOT shrink just because there are many of them: the last weight is exactly as big, as thick and as heavy-looking as the first. Each weight alone looks like it weighs several kilograms, each chain is pulled bar-straight and taut, and at a glance every single one looks crushingly, unmistakably heavy, the chains hanging freely in the air, clear of her neck and shoulders, with even the longest chain and its weight ending no lower than the level of her collarbones, never below them and never resting on her chest or body. Because the load is shared between three openings, the weight pulls each earlobe down only very slightly into a soft, healthy loop of skin, a barely noticeable natural droop that is just enough to show the weights are heavy; the lobe never stretches long, never tears or collapses and never hangs down to her neck or shoulder, her head stays upright, and the skin stays smooth and intact, fully healed, with no tearing, no wound, no blood and no redness. The face and ear jewelry is real pastel-enamelled gold set with white pearls, pastel gemstones, hearts and stars, while the hanging weights are always rough, matte, unpolished heavy metal in mixed materials (lead, tin, gold, silver, bronze, copper, brass and iron), sitting in real, calm, healthy skin — no redness, no swelling, no irritation — with a small natural warm shadow under each piece. Every piece stays at least a finger's width from the eyeballs, and no chain or bar crosses the eyes.

Piercing depth: every bar and surface bar is embedded in the skin — its middle runs beneath the skin so only its two end studs show on the surface, the skin between them faintly raised over the hidden bar, with a small warm shadow at each end and nothing lying on top of the skin like a sticker. Every ring passes through a small healed opening in the skin, the skin visible through the loop, and every stud sits through the skin with its back hidden. Where a bar, ring or stud goes through the ear, the lip, the nostril or the brow, it passes through the real tissue with the skin wrapping snugly around it.

Hair: her hair is swept back behind both ears, leaving both ears, her jawline and her neck fully visible so every hanging piece is in clear view.

Lighting: MANDATORY pure pitch black void background only, absolutely NO studio backdrop NO texture NO grey NO gradient. A soft frontal light on her face and ears, so the glints on every piece of metal read clearly against her skin; a thin cool rim light along the hair and shoulders. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
